issues.title: Implement the operations page layout
issues.scope: The structural shell of the page that makes this project a real Sorokeep showcase. FR-23 is explicit that it shows genuine data, so every section here must be wired to a real source rather than placeholder content.
acceptance: Layout matches the approved E13-06 wireframe with sections for TTL health, guard activity, alerts and admin actions
The page is viewable without a wallet — it shows system state rather than user data
Loading and error states use the shared components
Responsive behaviour follows E13-11; the dense tables must not force horizontal page scroll
No section renders fabricated or sample data, even temporarily
nonGoals: Individual sections are the following issues.

issues.title: Display TTL health per monitored entry
issues.scope: The core of the showcase: current TTL for the instance entry, the WASM entry and, if E10-04 found it workable, individual vault entries. What this page can honestly show depends on that finding.
acceptance: Each monitored entry shows its remaining TTL in ledgers and approximate real time
Entries approaching their threshold are visually distinguished, without relying on colour alone
Instance and WASM entries are distinguished from individual vault entries
If per-entry vault tracking proved impractical in E10-04, the page states that plainly rather than implying coverage that does not exist — an honest gap is better than a misleading display
Sorokeep being unreachable renders a clear state rather than an empty table
nonGoals: No TTL polling from the frontend; data comes from the backend.

issues.title: Display guard policy and auto-extension history
issues.scope: Show that auto-extension is configured and actually happening. A guard that is configured but has never fired looks identical to one that is broken unless the history is visible.
acceptance: The active guard policy is shown, including thresholds and whether auto-extension is enabled
Recent extensions are listed with entry, ledger, and cost in XLM
Cumulative extension cost is shown, since that is the number that makes the ongoing commitment concrete
A guard configured but never triggered shows that state explicitly rather than an empty list
No secret or key material is displayed anywhere, only the public key if relevant
nonGoals: No guard configuration from the UI.

issues.title: Display the Sorokeep alert timeline
issues.scope: Threshold crossings paired with their resolutions, so the page reads as a history of incidents rather than a list of disconnected events.
acceptance: Alerts are listed newest first with entry, severity, threshold values and time
A crossing and its later resolution render as one resolved incident, not two rows
An unresolved crossing is visually distinct from a resolved one
Both the alert's own timestamp and when this backend received it are available, so a delivery delay is visible
An empty timeline states that no alerts have fired rather than appearing broken

issues.title: Display admin action history
issues.scope: The only place in the entire system where pause, upgrade, whitelist changes and admin transfers are visible. Sorokeep does not track application events, so if this page does not show them, nothing does.
acceptance: All seven action types render with actor, approximate time and their specific details
Upgrades are prominent and display the new wasm hash, so it can be compared against what was expected
Admin transfers show both the previous and new address
Config updates show the old and new lock bounds where both are known
Filtering by action type is available
An empty history states that no admin actions have occurred
nonGoals: No admin controls; the API is read-only.

issues.title: Display ingestion status and data freshness
issues.scope: Every figure on this page comes from the cache. Without a freshness indicator a visitor cannot tell whether an empty alert timeline means all is well or that ingestion stopped two days ago.
acceptance: Current lag is shown in human terms alongside the last successful ingestion cycle
A detected history gap is surfaced prominently, stating which ledger range is missing
The healthy state is shown unobtrusively rather than omitted, so its absence is unambiguous
Displayed at the top of the page, since it qualifies everything below it
Backend unreachable is distinguished from backend reachable but lagging

issues.title: Display storage cost information
issues.scope: Surface what keeping this contract's storage alive actually costs. It is the most honest part of the showcase — a vault product's viability depends on upkeep staying below what it holds.
acceptance: Cumulative extension cost to date is shown in XLM
Cost per entry and the current entry count are shown, so the relationship to scale is visible
A projection is included, clearly labelled as an estimate, based on the measurements in docs/storage-costs.md
The funding account's balance is shown if available, since the guard stops when it empties
Figures come from real measurements, never from hardcoded estimates
nonGoals: No cost alerting from the frontend.

issues.title: Handle Sorokeep being unavailable on the operations page
issues.scope: Depending on what E10-12 chose, live TTL data may come from a source that is not always reachable. Stored alerts remain available regardless, so the page should degrade to those rather than going blank.
acceptance: Sections depending on live Sorokeep data show an unavailable state while sections backed by stored data still render
The distinction is explained to the visitor rather than leaving them to infer it
The page never renders a partial figure that could be mistaken for a complete one
Verified by actually making the Sorokeep source unreachable and screenshotting the result
nonGoals: No caching of live TTL data in the frontend.

issues.title: Add a contract information panel
issues.scope: Show which contract this deployment is actually pointed at. A frontend configured against the wrong contract id currently produces an empty but working-looking app, and this panel makes that immediately obvious.
acceptance: Contract id, network, current admin and current lock bounds are displayed
The contract id links to a block explorer for the correct network
Paused state is shown with the ledger at which it changed
A mismatch between the frontend's configured contract and the backend's is surfaced as a prominent warning rather than silently preferring one
The running contract version from version() is shown if available, so an upgrade is visible here too

issues.title: Apply accessibility requirements to the operations page
issues.scope: This page is the densest in the product and leans heavily on status indication, which makes it the most likely to fail the E13-10 requirements.
acceptance: Every status — TTL health, alert severity, freshness — is distinguishable without colour
Tables have proper headers and are navigable by keyboard
Filter controls are labelled and operable by keyboard
An automated accessibility check is run against the route with results pasted; remaining issues are fixed or listed with reasons
Dynamically updating regions are announced appropriately rather than changing silently

issues.title: Apply responsive layout to the operations page
issues.scope: Several dense tables that will not fit a narrow screen without the deliberate treatment E13-11 specified.
acceptance: The page is usable at the narrowest supported width with no horizontal page scroll
Tables use the specified narrow-screen treatment; columns E13-11 marked as never-hidden remain visible
The freshness indicator stays visible at every width, since it qualifies everything else
Verified at each specified breakpoint and the results listed

issues.title: Add component tests for the operations page
issues.scope: Cover the states most likely to appear at the wrong moment: unavailable sources, empty data, and degraded freshness.
acceptance: Each section is tested in populated, empty, loading and error states
Alert correlation is tested: a crossing with a resolution renders as one resolved incident
The unavailable-Sorokeep state is tested, asserting stored data still renders
The gap-detected state is tested
Tests use stubbed API responses; no network required
nonGoals: No browser end-to-end tests; those are E17.

issues.title: Verify the operations page shows genuinely real data
issues.scope: FR-23 states this is a genuine showcase page, not a mockup. That claim needs verification against the live system, because a page that renders plausible-looking data from stubs is exactly what this requirement exists to prevent.
acceptance: The page is loaded against the live backend and the deployed testnet contract; capture a screenshot
Every displayed figure is traced to its real source and the trace recorded — TTL values reconciled against sorokeep status, admin actions against real transactions, alerts against real deliveries
At least one real alert is visible in the timeline, from an actual Sorokeep delivery rather than a test insert
Any section that cannot yet show real data is listed explicitly as a known gap rather than filled with something plausible
The screenshot and traces go into docs/ttl-findings.md as the evidence behind the showcase claim

issues.title: Final frontend polish and consistency pass
issues.scope: A pass across all four views for the inconsistencies that accumulate when pages are built by different people against the same design: divergent loading treatments, inconsistent number formatting, error messages in three voices.
acceptance: Every view uses the shared loading, error and empty components rather than local variants
Amount formatting is identical across all views for the same value; verify by displaying one known balance in each place and comparing
Error messages are consistent in tone and all actionable, with no raw error strings reaching the user
Every route is checked against its approved wireframe and deviations are listed with reasons
`npm run build` produces a clean production build with zero TypeScript errors and no console warnings on any route
nonGoals: No new features. No redesign — deviations go back to E13 rather than being decided here.
